articles.title: Former James Bond Endorses Robert Pattinson as 007 16 Years After Playing His Dad in a Wild Movie
articles.summary: Robert Pattinson's casting as James Bond has gotten the official seal of approval from Pierce Brosnan. The Irish actor was previously responsible for starting a new era of 007 himself back in the '90s, kicking off a resurgence that helped keep the character relevant at a time when Austin Powers' mockery of the franchise began […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Robert Pattinson's casting as James Bond has gotten the official seal of approval from Pierce Brosnan. The Irish actor was previously responsible for starting a new era of 007 himself back in the '90s, kicking off a resurgence that helped keep the character relevant at a time when Austin Powers ' mockery of the franchise began to make the Bond team consider drastic changes . Though Pierce Brosnan previously endorsed Callum Turner for the job when rumors began circulating he was up for the part, the star has now given a thumbs up to Pattinson, and it doesn't hurt they played father and son once before.

"Dear Robert, Welcome to the world of Bond," Brosnan wrote in a post on social media. "You are going to be magnificent. I have fond memories of our time together making 'Remember Me.' It has been a joy to watch you create a remarkable body of work and to go from strength to strength. Enjoy the ride. Grá mor, Pierce." For those unfamiliar, Remember Me was the 2010 romance-drama featuring Pattinson that has become something of a meme in recent years, because of the finale reveal confirming the story culminates in the 9/11 terrorist attacks, which results in he death of Pattinson's character.

View this post on Instagram Robert Pattin's 007 Gets Seal of Approval From Pierce Brosnan Robert Pattinson becomes just the second new James Bond of the 21st century and only the seventh actor ever to play the part when his casting was confirmed, putting him in pretty rare company in Hollywood. That in mind, 2010's Remember Me is now notable for an extra piece of trivia beyond its surprise ending, as there's zero precedent that two actors who played the part of James Bond have been in the same movie at all, though only one had the already played the part at the time.

Though it may seem surprising that former James Bond actors wouldn't be in the same projects, one has to remember that becoming 007 means a certain level of elevation for a performer. Even if your films are something of black sheep in the family, like Dalton's two movies, you don't go from playing James Bond to then being fourth or fifth on the call sheet anymore.

To that end, it's easy to see why Bonds don't share the screen at all, and it's why their rare appearances together are so special. One of the only times this happened was back in 1989 when former James Bond stars Sean Connery and Roger Moore presented the Acadmy Award for Best Supporting Actor alongside Michael Caine. The fact that these two previously played the role set them up to rib Caine for not ever having the role himself.

Brosnan is just the latest former James Bond star to welcome Pattinson into the club, as Australian actor George Lazenby, who played 007 in just one movie, 1969's On Her Majesty's Secret Service, was quick to welcome him "to the most exclusive club in the world" telling the actor to "remember to enjoy yourself." Only two other former James Bond actors are still living at this point, Timothy Dalton and Daniel Craig, neither of whom has issued any kind of statement about Pattinson joining their ranks as 007.

No official word has been revealed about a production timeline for Robert Pattinson's debut as James Bond, but with Denis Villeneuve directing and a script by Steven Knight, it seems likely that cameras will roll sooner rather than later.

articles.summary: IMAGE COURTESY OF ITV A remake of The Prisoner is being attempted again, and this time it looks like it'll actually work. […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A remake of The Prisoner is being attempted again, and this time it looks like it'll actually work. The groundbreaking 1967 TV series , about a secret agent trapped in a bizarre seaside village meant to disorient and interrogate him, memorably used surreal imagery and a Kafka-esque plot, and has been a cult hit ever since. AMC and ITV collaborated on an American TV remake in 2009, but reviews and ratings were not kind. Movies have been attempted over the years, by Simon West in 2001, Ridley Scott in 2016 , and Christopher Nolan, in 2009 and 2024 .

Now, however, Transformers producer Don Murphy will be bringing it to Prime Video, according to The Hollywood Reporter . Given that Prime has managed to bring back Spider-Noir , Blade Runner , and The Lord of the Rings as streaming shows, this version of The Prisoner seems likely to happen, and is said to be a priority. Murphy recently remade the faux-snuff film Faces of Death into a modern, dramatic horror movie. He's apparently a lifelong fan of the original, and is looking for showrunners now.

Like many surreal sci-fi shows, The Prisoner didn't have a huge budget for special effects, so it often went weird instead, famously using giant balloons to represent security robots. It all added to the disorienting effect that was meant to make the titular character (Patrick McGoohan) confess and spill his secrets. The resort-like prison called The Village was loosely based on an isolated World War II installation in Scotland, near Inverness. The prisoner himself, known only as Number Six, would occasionally foil the authorities but never escape. Sixties style color schemes and fashions made it look hip at the time, but mark it as even more strangely off-kilter today. Broadcast in black and white originally in the UK, it was shot in color for the U.S. market. Maybe they could do both on Prime, as Spider-Noir did.

As the producer of the Transformers movies, including Rise of the Beasts , which ended in a G.I. Joe tease, Murphy has to be aware that Danny McBride's upcoming G.I. Joe reboot is based on a Prisoner -inspired storyline , "There's No Place Like Springfield." It seems safe to say that Duke, or whichever Joe is captured, will break out of Springfield by the end, but if Murphy's reboot is successful, it's more likely to go the other way — indeed, the finale of the original answered very little and left more questions than answers, infuriating fans at the time. Nonetheless, the similar hook probably helps both projects.

Murphy is also working on a reboot of Buck Rogers (another project that has had several failed attempts prior ), and presumably the next Transformers movie, which is bringing back original director Michael Bay. His 2011 Real Steel was an adaptation of a Twilight Zone episode based on a Richard Matheson short story; Murphy's genre TV fandom, and determination to adapt that which he loves, knows few bounds.

Are you interested in a new take on The Prisoner ? Did you watch the original, or the 2009 version? Let's build a village of comments below.

articles.title: 5 WildStorm Teams That Could Become Major Players in the DC Universe
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics Being a fan of DC Comics is amazing right now. The publisher is putting out the best superhero comics in the industry and no one else is even close. Readers love what they're doing with their multiverse and they've rewarded the company by buying their books. DC has destroyed Marvel's market share advantage and it […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Being a fan of DC Comics is amazing right now. The publisher is putting out the best superhero comics in the industry and no one else is even close. Readers love what they're doing with their multiverse and they've rewarded the company by buying their books. DC has destroyed Marvel's market share advantage and it feels like everything they release is amazing. They are on fire and the best part is that they aren't even digging all deep into their bag of tricks. The company has access to many of the best characters ever, including the heroes of the defunct Wildstorm Universe, Jim Lee's old Image imprint.

I'm not going to pretend that Wildstorm comics were some amazing books full of unique characters; it was the '90s and the characters were very much of their time. However, that doesn't mean that there aren't some awesome Wildstorm characters. One place where Wildstorm always excelled was team books. There are some awesome Wildstorm teams that could be brought into the DC Multiverse and they would make a huge splash. These five Wildstorm teams can be major players in DC Comics, showing that the company can spin anything into a success.

The Authority is the most well-known Wildstorm team, to the extent that once upon a time, we were told the DCU was going to make a movie starring them. The team was created by Warren Ellis, who had taken over Stormwatch and put them through their paces, eventually spinning that group into the Authority. The Authority was a Justice League pastiche, with Apollo, Midnighter, Swift, the Doctor, the Engineer, Jack Hawksmoor, and Jenny Sparks each fitting into various Justice League roles. However, unlike that team, they were known for being proactive, ending threats before they could hurt anyone.

The Ellis/Hitch run was huge, but the Mark Millar/Frank Quitely run on The Authority took them to a new level of popularity. However, delays hurt the book's momentum and it would fade away (although not before doing the first gay marriage in superhero comics). Since then, DC has tried to bring the team back several times, with the most popular attempt having been Superman and the Authority and "Warworld Saga" in 2021. However, this wasn't the original version of the group, it was a modified one. If DC brought back the old school team and put them in big, bloody, crude adventures again, that book would sell like hotcakes.

War comics were quite popular back in the Silver Age and Marvel would eventually start doing spy comics in the '60s with Nick Fury. Paramilitary groups became a huge part of comics in the years to come and the Image guys were no different. They created numerous black ops teams for their respective books (it's kind of funny to think at one point, all the Image heroes were in one universe and it was one that had a thousand versions of SHIELD). The Wildstorm books would start to hint at Team 7, a group of (maybe) supersoldiers that fought back in the day with ties to the current generation of superhumans.

Team 7 was the origin explanation for characters like Grifter and Deathwatch, but it was never very popular. DC has tried to use Team 7 in the past and failed, but there's no time like the present. So many of the Wildstorm characters aren't being used right now, so it would honestly be a snap to bring back Team 7 or just to take the idea – a group of soldiers experimented on with alien genetic material back during the Cold War – and use it in new ways. It's just a plain good idea that you can use for just about anything.

Stormwatch was introduced in 1993 and was the second Wildstorm team. Stormwatch was kind of the Wildstorm equivalent of SHIELD (well, the one that wasn't International Operations, which was also the SHIELD of Wildstorm; see what I was talking about above?), the team sent to deal with superpowered threats across the globe from their space station headquarters. Their book was merely fine until Warren Ellis took over, spinning his run out of the Wildstorm crossover with the Alien franchise, which would eventually lead to the Authority.

When the New 52 dawned , DC tried to use a lot of Wildstorm characters and concepts, with Stormwatch in their satellite, protecting the Earth. The team lasted 31 issues and then vanished. Recently, DC tried to do something similar in Batman: The Brave and the Bold , with Stormwatch being one of its serials. We know it exists in the current DC Multiverse, so all they have to do is dust it off, take it out of the nine dollar a month anthology book (I was subbed to it for a while), throw some high-levels creators on it, and go to town.

I'm going to level with you as someone whose job it is to type – I hate the WildC.A.T.s. Now, I love the team's comics; I was into them because I was a Jim Lee fan back then and then Lee got writers like Chris Claremont, James Robinson, and the incomparable Alan Moore (Moore's WildC.A.T.s was my first Moore comic), making the book even better. The problem is their name is annoying to type which, for the purposes of this joke, I'm going to pretend is the only reason they aren't more popular and not that they were mostly just an X-Men pastiche with potential that only reached it rarely.

The team's whole thing was that they were Kherubim or part Kherubim, an alien race that looked like humans with superpowers, that crashlanded on Earth millennia ago while battling their enemies Daemonites, the Kherubim protecting the Earth from the possessive power of the demonic aliens. The characters were simple but cool and the cliche origin was actually used pretty well by numerous creators (especially Moore). The team was recently brought back by Matthew Rosenberg and Stephen Segovia for a short but excellent series and it's time for more. DC has the talent to make them as popular as they were back in the day.

So, I doubt you know this about me, but I'm old. I was a teen in the '90s and Wildstorm was my favorite Image imprint. However, I only bought from the newsstand back then, so I missed out on one of the biggest Wildstorm/Image books of the decade – Gen13 . The five-issue series introduced Fairchild, Freefall, Grunge, Burnout, and Rainmaker, teens given superpowers in an experiment, their name coming from being the 13th generation of Americans. J. Scott Campbell's art hooked readers and suddenly Gen13 was massively popular.

Over the years, DC has tried to make the team work again, but has never brought them whole cloth into the DC Multiverse. It's about time to make that happen. '90s teens like me have money and would love to see a new version of an old favorite. Make them zoomers, get a younger creative team (something the company has been excelling at), and let them go to town with the book. Gen13 is a relic of the '90s, but like the most important relics, it will always have some value.

What Wildstorm teams do you think could make DC even more popular? Which ones do you think have potential to be something in the 21st century? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.title: 'Ramayana' Star Sai Pallavi, Ravi Kishan's 'Spider-Man' Anecdote, Grammy Winner Ricky Kej Light Up International Film Festival of India Opening in Goa
articles.summary: The 57th International Film Festival of India opened in Goa on Friday, with "Lagaan" director Ashutosh Gowariker setting out a "Stories Without Borders" program in his first year as festival director and Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant renewing his push for a film city in the state. Paweł Pawlikowski's "Fatherland," which shared the best director […]
articles.content:
The 57th International Film Festival of India opened in Goa on Friday, with "Lagaan" director Ashutosh Gowariker setting out a "Stories Without Borders" program in his first year as festival director and Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant renewing his push for a film city in the state.

Paweł Pawlikowski's "Fatherland," which shared the best director prize at Cannes this year, opened the festival. The ceremony at the Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Indoor Stadium began with the national anthem "Jana Gana Mana" and national song "Vande Mataram," followed by a ceremonial lamp lighting with Sawant, National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) chair G. Krishna Kumar, Gowariker and several other dignitaries. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'Hold Onto Me' Director Myrsini Aristidou Kicks Off Historic Oscar Campaign for Sundance Audience Award Winner: 'I Really Feel Like We're Underdogs'

Bollywood star Kartik Aaryan was in attendance, along with Sai Pallavi , who plays Sita in Nitesh Tiwari's blockbuster " Ramayana ." Jury chairs Aanand L. Rai ("Tanu Weds Manu"), who heads the international jury, and filmmakers Madhur Bhandarkar and Himanshu Sekhar Khatua, who led the Indian Panorama feature and non-feature juries respectively, were also in the audience. The festival runs through Nov. 28.

Three-time Grammy winner Ricky Kej set the tone with "A World of Cinema Through Music," an orchestral performance built around a medley of film themes played with Indian instruments. It moved from "The Godfather," "Parasite" and "Rashomon" to "The Lord of the Rings," Satyajit Ray's "Pather Panchali," "Doctor Zhivago," "The Good, the Bad and the Ugly," "La Bamba," Gowariker's own "Lagaan" and "Mission: Impossible 2." Kej returned later with a set mixing musical traditions from Italy, Mongolia, the U.S., India and the U.A.E. A peacock dance, symbolizing the festival's Golden Peacock award, also featured on the program. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Goa has been IFFI's permanent home since 2004, and its streets and landmarks have turned up in films such as "Dil Chahta Hai" and "Dear Zindagi." "But our ambition goes further," Sawant said. "We want Goa to become the place where the films are produced and completed."

The state's plans include a proposed film city with facilities for pre-production, post-production, VFX and film education, which Sawant said would encourage local filmmaking, draw filmmakers from across India and open new avenues for young Goan creative professionals. He has raised the idea at earlier editions of the festival, seeking central government support for a Goa film city at the 2021 opening ceremony. Sawant also pointed to the Goa Regulation of Film Shooting Act 2021 and an online single-window permit system run by the Entertainment Society of Goa, and said the state's film financing scheme for Goan producers is being revised to cover newer formats and digital productions. With virtual production, AI, animation and VFX changing how films are made, he said Goa wants a stake in that next phase.

Gowariker, the Oscar-nominated director of "Lagaan," "Swades" and "Jodhaa Akbar," took the job in May. He told the audience that until now he had only experienced festivals as a filmmaker who flies in with a film, does a Q&A and leaves, and that his team shaped this edition by asking what stories actually do for people.

"We live in a time when we are more connected than ever, and yet it has also become very easy to stay inside our own circle," Gowariker said. "Borders today are not only lines on a map. They're also habits. A story is one of the few things that can cross such a line without a passport."

The international program comprises 159 films from 86 countries, picked from more than 1,400 submissions, according to Gowariker, alongside 76 Indian films in 18 languages. Romanian director Alina Șerban's "I Matter," a Romania-Germany-Belgium production, is the mid-festival film, and Singaporean director Anthony Chen's "We Are All Strangers" closes the event. Spain is this year's Country of Honor and Russia the Partner Country. A showcase of 21 films from BRICS nations, a first for the festival, opens with "Ramayana" on Nov. 22.

Fifteen films compete for five awards in the International Competition. Prize money across the festival's jury awards totals INR1.36 crore ($147,000), including INR51 lakh ($55,000) and the Golden Peacock for best film. Rai's jury also includes Romanian director Bogdan Mureșanu, Venezuelan sound designer María Alejandra Rojas, Thai director Ratchapoom Boonbunchachoke and Argentine director Sol Berruezo Pichon-Rivière. Eighteen titles in the lineup are their countries' Oscar submissions. The program also counts nine world premieres, two international premieres, 24 Asian premieres and 116 India premieres. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The Indian Panorama section brings 25 features and 20 non-features from across the country, chosen by Bhandarkar's and Khatua's juries. It opens with Aditya Dhar's Hindi-language "Dhurandhar" and Leena Yadav's "Becoming," a film in Ladakhi. A curated package of 15 Goan films and six award winners from the 19th Mumbai International Film Festival complete the Indian slate.

Gowariker also spoke about the WAVES Film Bazaar, the festival's market, where buyers, programmers and producers from Paris, Busan and London mix with filmmakers such as a young director from Guwahati in northeastern India who had ridden a train for two days to get there.

"Sometimes a great deal of cinema begins with someone saying, 'Come, let's have a coffee,' and the other person saying, 'Sure, I have ten minutes,'" he said. "Three hours later, there's a co-production."

On the heritage front, the festival marks the centenary of Polish director Andrzej Wajda and revisits the work of Prem Nazir, Suryakant Mandhare, Raj Kumar, Uttam Kumar, Shakti Samanta, composers O.P. Nayyar and Ravi across Hindi, Bengali, Marathi and Malayalam cinema. "Lagaan" celebrates its 25th anniversary at the festival.

Two new sections, Animation and Films About Films, feature Brad Bird's "Ray Gunn" and Barnaby Thompson's documentary "Maverick: The Epic Adventures of David Lean." Women directed 52 films in the international lineup and first-time filmmakers 62. Of the 21 titles across the festival's three competitions, 10 are by women and 12 are debuts.

Chanchal Kumar, secretary of India's Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, said, "A border may define where a story begins, it need not define how far that story can travel."

Chief guest Ravi Kishan, a Bhojpuri star and second-term Member of Parliament from Gorakhpur, looked back on a 34-year career spanning almost 700 films in Hindi, Bhojpuri, Telugu, Kannada, Tamil, Gujarati and Marathi, including Kiran Rao's "Laapataa Ladies," India's Oscar entry.

"Many years ago, I had the chance to lend my voice to Spider-Man as Tobey Maguire, and what, in Bhojpuri!" Kishan said. "Imagine there was no border and it was a blockbuster in Bihar."

Gowariker urged the audience to spend part of the nine days on a film they would not normally pick. "Watch at least one film in a language you do not understand, a film from a country you have not visited, and by a filmmaker whose name you have not heard," he said. "Let the subtitles do their work. I think you will find that the border was never as wide as you thought."

It's time to head back to Panem with " The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping " this weekend.

The latest entry in the Lionsgate series has made $21 million in Thursday previews and early screenings Wednesday at the box office. It's expected to open with more than $100 million at the box office, though the studio is more cautiously predicting an $85 million debut. However, some estimates put the sixth "Hunger Games" movie even higher at $125 million due to the franchise's fandom and the return of some fan-favorite characters. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

If the opening crosses $100 million, it'll be one of five movies this year to surpass the milestone and join "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" ($360 million), "Toy Story 5" ($159 million), "The Super Mario Galaxy Movie" ($131 million) and "The Odyssey" ($123 million).

"Sunrise on the Reaping" comes three years after the last "Hunger Games" prequel, "The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes." The 2023 movie made $5.75 million in previews and opened to $44 million. It ended its run with $363 million globally, making it a success against its $100 million budget. "Sunrise on the Reaping" should open closer to the original 2010s franchise starring Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson, which will help as it carries a $150 million budget.

The first "Hunger Games" debuted to $152 million in 2012, with 2013’s “Catching Fire” as the highest opening with $158 million and an $865 million final global tally. The final two-part "Mockingjay" movies opened with $121 million for "Part One" and $102 million for "Part Two."

"Sunrise on the Reaping" tells the story of young Haymitch Abernathy, played by Woody Harrelson in the original movies and now portrayed by Joseph Zada. The movie also stars Mckenna Grace, Ralph Fiennes, Kiernan Culkin, Glenn Close, Elle Fanning, Jesse Plemons and more.

articles.content:
French actor Gérard Depardieu is facing a new complaint alleging rape and sexual assault during the filming of Guillaume Nicloux’s “Thalasso” in 2018, according to an investigation published by Mediapart on Thursday.

The complaint also names Nicloux, who directed the film, and Michel Houellebecq, one of France's most celebrated novelists who starred alongside Depardieu.

The alleged incident took place on Dec. 11, 2018, during a scene that was filmed by the movie’s cameras, although the screenplay did not include any sexual activity, according to Mediapart. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The complainant, an actor, alleges that she was raped by Depardieu and sexually assaulted by Houellebecq in the presence of Nicloux, whom she accuses of complicity.

Nicloux told Mediapart that he had not witnessed “any coercion, verbal or physical opposition” during the filming of the scene. He said he was distressed to learn that the actor had experienced what she described without his realizing it, and acknowledged having apologized to her afterward. Depardieu’s lawyers, Delphine Meillet and David-Olivier Kaminski, told French radio station RTL that they were unaware of the proceedings.

The complaint was filed in May 2025, shortly after Depardieu stood trial for sexually assaulting two women on the set of the 2021 film “Les Volets verts.” The new allegations come just days after Depardieu withdrew his appeal against his conviction in that case, making his 18-month suspended prison sentence final.

In a statement titled “J’entends” (“I Hear”) released Monday, the 77-year-old actor accepted responsibility for his conviction and offered “deep and sincere apologies” to those who “may have suffered as a result.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“Justice has spoken. I have been found guilty. I accept this and take responsibility for this conviction,” Depardieu wrote, according to Le Monde.

His lawyer, Meillet, said the actor had undergone a period of reflection and wanted to avoid putting the complainants through another trial.

“He is a man who has come a long way, who has reached a turning point, who has taken a big step after a long period of reflection and maturation,” Meillet said. “He wanted to avoid making the complainants go through another hearing, or having to go through one himself.”

Depardieu also faces a separate rape case involving actress Charlotte Arnould, who accused him of assaulting her in 2018. An investigating judge has ordered the actor to stand trial, a decision he is contesting. The Paris appeals court is expected to rule on Nov. 26 on whether the case will proceed to trial. articles.summary: Courtesy of Rockstar Games Cheats are an underrated part of Grand Theft Auto 6, with each one allowing you to modify your gameplay in different ways to make experiences easier or harder. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Cheats are an underrated part of Grand Theft Auto 6 , with each one allowing you to modify your gameplay in different ways to make experiences easier or harder. Unlocked by reaching different points of progression in the story, there are over 60 different cheats in the game, with each serving a unique purpose to alter specific features. For players who complete various in-game challenges, these cheats act as rewards to keep things exciting, making GTA 6 a more personalized experience for those who've earned the right to change it.

Before you can use any cheat at all, you have to at least beat the main story of GTA 6 once, and unlock any of the multiple endings tied to it. Unlike past GTA titles , you can't just activate cheats right away if you know them, you must first go through the realistic narrative of the game before stretching it to its limits. Other cheats are locked by other limitations, such as finishing the aforementioned challenges or not being able to save your game once you activate them in different circumstances.

The good news with GTA 6 's cheat restrictions is that you probably unlocked a variety of them as your first playthrough continued. Once you complete the story, a new Cheats tab will pop up on your Progress menu, letting you see every cheat in the game and what you have to do to unlock it. Several should already be at your disposal, even if they won't help you unlock any trophies or achievements once activated. Without saves or achievement progress, these cheats become fairly niche, but still add plenty of fun to the game outside of what it presented normally.

Similar to getting a 6-Star wanted level in GTA 6 , cheats are something you have to pursue actively. The table(s) below go over all the different cheats available in GTA 6 , what you need to do to unlock them, and what they do once activated:

As you can see, most of these cheat codes are for applying unique screen filter effects or simply spawning vehicles near you. However, the best cheats are typically those like Max Ammo or Attack Force, which enhance your combat gameplay to complete challenges. Being able to artificially raise your Heat, keep your Focus, or increase your Wanted level are also great, along with some other cheats that prevent you from taking damage from falling. Any cheats that help you skip the limitations of resources are worth at least unlocking through GTA 6 's milestones revealed through the Progress menu.

To activate any of these cheats, you need to use Jason or Lucia's in-game phone in the same way cheats have worked in other GTA games. Once you pull out your phone, you have to use the D-pad on your controller to input the commands listed in the tables from the previous section. This means every combination works exactly the same on both PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, but if the game ever comes out on PC, it could change. Holding the left shoulder input on your controller, then pressing the input for the right shoulder button should bring up the cheats menu, where the D-pad combination can begin.

As of this time of writing, no other dial numbers or phone codes have worked as alternate cheats like they did in GTA 5 , which is likely intentional. Nothing happens when you input any of the GTA 5 phone codes, but perhaps that will change as the game evolves over time. New cheats may arrive through DLC, the addition of GTA Online , or other updates to Grand Theft Auto 6 , turning this already celebrated game into something players can adjust even more to their preferences.

articles.title: All's Fair in Love and 'War': Creator George Kay Explains His Ruling on Morgan and Carla's Divorce
articles.summary: The creator of the HBO/Sky legal drama anthology opens up to THR about why he settled (no pun intended) on a more hopeful ending to an acrimonious divorce, that recurring Keanu Reeves quote and how the newly unmasked mole will factor into season two.
articles.content:
[This story contains MAJOR spoilers from the War finale.]

As the old saying goes, all’s fair in love and War .

By the end of the first season of the HBO/Sky legal drama, tech billionaire Morgan Henderson ( Dominic West ) and film star Carla Duval ( Sienna Miller ) have officially dissolved their marriage. Over the course of eight episodes, often at the behest of their own conniving lawyers, the estranged exes (and co-parents to her child from a previous relationship) have gone to scorched-earth extremes to come out on top: honey-trapping to dig up evidence of infidelity, springing divorce papers on a red carpet, getting a prenup thrown out, shifting assets out of reach, planting a mole inside the opposing law firm, and airing the other’s adultery on a major talk show. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV Archie Renaux on 'War's Resident -- and Misunderstood -- Bad Boy Movies 'Madden' Review: Nicolas Cage and Christian Bale Go for Broke in a Cartoonish Biopic From David O. Russell That's Strictly for Football Fanatics

But in the end, Morgan and Carla, who have ironically grown closer than they have in years by legally separating, decide to take matters into their own hands at the end of a tense two-day trial. Before a judge can rule, the pair strike a settlement that gives each a fair share of Zephyr, the social-media platform that Carla named and Morgan founded after hearing about her harsh experiences of being scrutinized online.

“One of the phrases that came up in the writers’ room was that this divorce is like the world’s most expensive couples therapy because by the end, they’re kind of closer together emotionally than they were at the start,” creator George Kay tells The Hollywood Reporter . Morgan and Carla are last seen walking arm-in-arm together on a beach in Normandy, where they first fell in love a decade ago. But, according to Kay, that doesn’t necessarily mean that the characters are back together again: “I think that they’re a happy, functioning, loving family, but they’re no longer a couple.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Below, Kay (best known to U.S. audiences for co-creating Netflix’s Lupin and Apple TV’s Hijack ) opens up to THR about why he settled on a more hopeful ending to an acrimonious divorce, the significance of a certain Keanu Reeves quote, and how Johnny (Archie Renaux) — the newly unmasked mole inside Carla’s law firm, Taylor & Byrne, who was secretly working for Morgan’s lawyers at the powerhouse firm Cathcarts all along — will factor into the show’s future.

Having already wrapped production on season two, which will focus on a defamation suit , Kay confirms that each season of War will focus on a different legal dispute with litigants represented by Cathcarts and Taylor & Byrne, complete with high-profile guest stars appearing for season-long arcs as clients.

Morgan and Carla could have settled out of court numerous times, but it isn’t until after their trial that they reach a settlement on their own terms, without the input of their lawyers or a judge. Did you always plan to end the case that way? Did you ever toy with a different ending in which one of them “wins”?

We liked that ending pretty early. The only way to find the truth about this relationship was for them to finally face up to each other. At the beginning of the show, the reason they’re splitting up is, of course, there are infidelities and bad behaviors, but it’s all a symptom of not spending time together. I think in these high-end worlds, that’s the thing that gets lost. People have lots of money, but they’re very time-poor. They don’t share their lives together, and that’s what’s driving them apart. And actually, what you see with this show is that [divorce] forces them back together, in a way. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

They spent eight hours scrapping, and I think if they’d been left further arguing, you wouldn’t like them. [That’s] not to say that our job is to make these people likable — because it really isn’t — but I did start to like them more and more. I wanted there to be a kind of score draw between the law firms and an outcome that went beyond the law, because the law manipulates the lives of these people — albeit very privileged, high-end, high-wealth lives. But no, we wanted the ending to have some heart and redemption for them. The big part of that as well was Flora’s input into that [dispute], reminding them of how they had overstretched their privilege, and she has a real impact on the outcome of the case.

You mentioned Flora Monroe (Rose Williams), Carla’s former co-star who has a one-night stand with Morgan to help Carla prove her estranged husband’s pattern of infidelity. Did you design the show then with the intention of bringing Flora back for the trial and having her talk some sense into Morgan and Carla on the stand?

It was one of the very first things [I decided], because I didn’t want to just use Flora as a character for the opening sequence and dispose of her in the way that Carla is almost doing. I wanted the show to be better than that, and I wanted her to learn a different lesson from that whole honey trap.

The conventional approach to telling a story about a separating couple would be to show the gradual breakdown of their relationship in flashbacks, but you avoided doing that with Morgan and Carla. Why did you choose to focus on them in the present day rather than dwelling on the past? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Because the divorce itself is a kind of review. To show the flashbacks of what really happened would be to betray the two sides of the argument. It’s not really about the truth; it’s about how different firms present [a version of the truth]. We can’t contest the truth as the audience in the way the lawyers are doing if we know that we have the objective facts.

With that in mind, what did you want the very few, brief glimpses of Morgan and Carla together — in the back of a car, in an elevator, in the back alley of the courthouse — to reveal about their relationship?

Whenever we saw them together, we tried to create a different dynamic. So in episode one, they are playing at being civil to each other, but they both know what’s coming. In episode two, there’s a strategy going on, so they’re both putting on a façade. They’re pretending to be decent people to deal with — all while they’re planning on ripping each other’s throats out, basically. When you see them later on in court, it can often be a case of the audience feeling, “Oh no, if he only knew how she felt, or if she only knew how he was feeling, but the lawyers have gotten in the way.” So you start to care for them more despite their lawyers.

Like you said, they could settle at any point. But the writers always felt like just before they could settle, something else comes along that spoils that as an outcome for them, and another set of lawyers doubles down. It’s this inevitable march to the end [where] there’s no way out of this trap that they’re in — it’s a self-imposed trap, but still a trap. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

You’ve talked about how War was inspired by other character-driven legal dramas like Ally McBeal , The Good Wife and Damages , but the distinctive twist that you brought to the genre was having a lawyer acting as a mole for opposing counsel. How early on in the development process did you decide that Johnny was going to be working as a double agent for Cathcarts?

When I was starting out, it was intended to be more of an out-and-out thriller. We’d referenced things like The Departed or All the President’s Men — that kind of corporate espionage and spy work within the workplace. I wanted to have a route into the show that was not just what we call in England the upper middle classes, which is the privileged strata of society that tends to [lead to] people in workplaces like Taylor & Byrne and Cathcarts.

I wanted to have this young kid who’s not from a privileged background trying to break into this privileged world. I had the idea of the two law firms before I had the idea of Johnny, and as he started to navigate the world of law firms trying to get a job interview, it started to become: “Hang on, which firm would I like him to be in?” I wanted him to be in Cathcarts, but I also wanted him to be in Taylor & Byrne, so I had the thought that maybe he could be in both because I think you want to have that connectivity between the characters.

The line “The simple act of paying attention can take you a long way” recurs throughout the first season in scenes with Cathcarts lawyer David Schill (Miles Jupp), but its significance doesn’t become clear until the end of episode six, when Johnny accidentally uses the quote in a courthouse conversation with Carla’s lawyer Serena (Phoebe Fox). That slip-up tips Serena off that Johnny is the mole who has been working for Cathcarts all along. What made you want to hinge so much of the series on a Keanu Reeves quote, and where did it come from? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

This is such a huge legal case that all of the resources on both sides have been plowed into it, and we liked the fact that the most simple, forgettable detail can be the thing that upsets the apple cart. We started talking about different phrases, and we called it the “Schill-ism.” David Schill is a man of quotes — and Miles Jupp’s a brilliant actor. He’s well-known as a comedian in the U.K., and I think he’s really surprised people. So we started to brainstorm what we call “Schill-isms” for David Schill — the sort of phrases he would use, little sayings, idioms.

It was nearly the phrase, “You don’t want to get ahead of your skis,” but we settled on a quotation because David Schill’s quite an Oxbridge kind of character and the sort of man who would drop in quotations. We wanted it to be something silly in that you think a man of Oxford or Cambridge would be quoting Keats or Wordsworth or Shakespeare. But, in fact, he drops in a quote that’s surprisingly profound for him, and the twist is it’s actually Keanu Reeves who said it.

We then looked at other Keanu Reeves quotes, and [we realized] he says quite a lot of profound things, so we were spoiled for choice. ( Laughs. ) “The simple act of paying attention can take you a long way” can apply to the technical preparations of a legal case. But I think [the quote] being so important and it being Keanu was just a great worlds colliding [moment] because Keanu Reeves is not something you’d [expect to] reference in this show about fusty British law firms, so it felt fun to us. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid6' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Were you always planning for Johnny to be outed as the mole? Did you consider having him exposed earlier or later in the show? Did you ever consider letting him get away with it?

We always felt he would be revealed at some point, and the most exciting point to reveal something is just at the moment you don’t need to reveal it for the case of the other characters. China Moo-Young, who directed the middle block — her final shot is the court doors closing on Johnny [after his slip-up], and the final act directed by Jen Sheridan is all in the court. So the idea that the second before the court case starts, all the other characters realize, “Hang on a sec. This is all completely compromised by the fact that we know who the mole is and he works for us,” felt like the hinge we wanted to create in the storyline.

That was quite clear to us, but I think there were layers of drama to find behind that. So the idea that there might be a mole warrants a whole episode. The idea that that mole then tries to obfuscate who it is and come up with theories about his friends being moles or throw other people under the bus for his own survival becomes an episode. We really enjoyed peeling that onion and stretching him out over three episodes. There’s the Ferrari twist [in episode five, where a stray mention of a Ferrari Testarossa on an asset disclosure list exposes that there’s a mole inside Taylor & Byrne in the first place]. There’s a bit like an episode of Traitors , and then there’s the final rumbling on him based on this silly quote that capsizes the whole thing. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid7' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Johnny spends the last two episodes of the season very much trying to atone and apologize for his mistakes while also fighting desperately for his own professional survival. Where did you want to leave him by the end of the season?

I wanted him to have a nice attempt to salvage his situation, and I think we do root for him and we do want him to succeed — or at least I did. I don’t know how you felt.

I could empathize with Johnny. I don’t necessarily agree with his choices, but I can see how his ambitions ultimately clouded his judgment. As a law student myself, I recognize some of my own classmates and future colleagues in him.

Also, it’s a tightrope act; once you’re up there, you’ve got to do what you need to stay up there. Okay, he tries to salvage it all, he grows a heart, and he becomes morally a bit more aware — but not before he’s tried to switch sides back to Cathcarts. It’s just a desperate game of survival for a kid that has been exploitative himself, but also has been exploited by the system. When we talked about Johnny at the very beginning of this process, Ben Taylor, our brilliant [first] director, and I were looking at a lot of early ’90s Tom Cruise films, like The Firm . All those kinds of Tom Cruise characters felt like they were likable — you rooted for them, but they could sometimes overstep; they’re a bit too keen, a bit too ambitious. That’s what we wanted to tread with Johnny. It’s that thing of, “Oh my God, I know a guy like that. I don’t dislike him, but he’s really chancing his arm here. In a way, given everything he’s been through, I kind of hope he sticks to the landing.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid8' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Can you confirm that Johnny will be back for season two?

He will be back for season two. We scoured London to find our Johnny Warren, and when Archie appeared, it was pretty clear to us that he was our guy. It’s a big ensemble show, so Johnny’s definitely a part of season two, and he’s got to pay for some of his decisions in season one.

But also coming into the foreground [next season at Taylor & Byrne], we have Emma Laird, who plays Molly, and Nick Mohammed [who plays Michael] — they came into the show knowing they were going to have a big season two. We were making promises to them at the casting stage saying, “Listen, if you come into this ensemble show, your story will come to the fore in the second season.” We were already planning that when we were casting those actors for season one.

That’s the real benefit of HBO and Sky backing us for a two-season order. We can start to layer in things, like the place where they buy their coffee from in season one — you see the cups with the logo on them — becomes a story point in season two. And in season two, they don’t talk on X; they talk on [Morgan’s social media platform] Zephyr. We continue the consistency of the world-building across the show, so it becomes a hermetically sealed thing.

Whereas the first season centered on a messy, high-profile divorce, the second will focus on a defamation suit. In success, will each season of War focus on a different kind of legal dispute?

Yes, totally. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid9' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Will Cathcarts and Taylor & Byrne be representing the litigants in each case?

The show’s built to be Cathcarts vs. Taylor & Byrne every season, and every season we’re going to have guest-star casting. So you have Dominic West divorcing Sienna Miller in season one. We have Marisa Tomei suing Kelly MacDonald for defamation in season two. [Marisa’s character, Avery Reed] flies over from London to claim damages for something that Jo MacNeil, Kelly’s character, has said. Of course, it means that the law firms have to pivot and bring their defamation lawyers to the fore, so there’s new casting to help with that.

The more it goes on, it’ll be an anthology show where different guest-star clients will come in and occupy the space for Cathcarts and Taylor & Byrne, and we come up with organic, believable ways that those firms come up against each other once again. But all the while, you’re just building on what I think of as a fantastic ensemble British cast. So, hopefully, you’re coming back to the show just as much for Phoebe Fox and Nina Sosanya [who plays Beatrice] as you are for the next guest stars that are going to appear.

Beyond the two-season order you were given, do you have a long-term plan for the series? Do you have a target number of seasons in mind?

I just want to keep the show going with amazing guest stars and be able to nurture those characters on both sides of Cathcarts and Taylor & Byrne over subsequent seasons. It’s always been designed to come back three, four seasons more. I’m not intending to find an ending to it. I want to keep expanding and developing that ensemble cast. So there should be all number of cases we can do to keep pushing those characters into more and more dramatic situations. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid10' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Johnny will certainly need to do a lot of work to get back in the good graces of Serena and Nick (James McArdle), who are last seen leaving the firm for Serena to give birth to their first child. What new layers of that relationship — and the rival firms — will you be exploring next season?

One of the great fun questions we had as writers was, “Could you work with your partner?” We may not have been lawyers or divorced, but we could all answer that question, and we all had very different views. [Serena and Nick] are still together and they are parents in season two. It starts three months after the end of season one. Of course, Serena is no longer working day-to-day; she’s on maternity leave. Maybe the harder thing than working with your partner is working with your partner when you are not there to see what they’re doing. So it means there’s even more friendly, loving rivalry between them as they try and work out how to manage a law firm when one of them is staying at home all day.

It’s been great to work with Phoebe because she was pregnant for real throughout season one, so then her maternity leave was real in season two. We do see Nick taking the lead a little bit more at the beginning of the season, if only because Phoebe Fox is on real maternity leave. ( Laughs .)

Also, we go home with the lawyers from Taylor & Byrne a lot more in season one, and it was always designed that in season two, we would emphasize the home lives of Cathcarts. You get to know why the really harsh lawyers are so harsh — and they’re not just born harsh; they have to be turned that way by life. You get to go home with them and understand who they really are as humans a lot more. So with Pip [Torrens, who plays St. John] and Nina, you’ll see much more of their [characters’] home lives. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid11' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

In the finale, Johnny tells Flora that he thinks it’s impossible to be a good lawyer and a good person. He shares the cynical view that lawyers — especially those working in family litigation — are only ever acting in their own best interests. I wouldn’t want your characters to speak for you, but after having made this show, how do you feel about lawyers?

It’s interesting because I have no more affection or dislike for lawyers than I do for any other walk of life. ( Laughs .) It’s all about different characters. I think the Johnny is more, “Is it possible [to be both]?” That’s the conundrum he faces, and for a character that’s going into the world of law and has been exposed to the dark tactics that are used in our show anyway, that question should come up. But I think the answer to that question is yes.

I think Johnny’s not all bad. It’s been interesting to see how the audience has over the series moved around on Johnny, who has a great likability but still does things that people object to and objectively are hard to love. We had a brilliant consultant, Catherine Bedford. She’s a really impressive woman and was very helpful to us, and then [we’d] hear about other family lawyers who can be awful to people. So you want to retain a bit of self-deprecation among the lawyers. They’ve got to do terrible things, but they’ve got to be aware of it; they’ve got to have that self-awareness. So I think that they know when they’re being bad, and that makes them more interesting than if they just were doing bad stuff. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid12' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

articles.title: Is Guillermo del Toro Making a Star Wars Movie? Oscar-Winning Director Responds to Rumors
articles.summary: IMAGE COURTESY OF NETFLIX If you were hoping rumors of Guillermo del Toro doing a Star Wars film or series were true, we have an update today from the director himself. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google If you were hoping rumors of Guillermo del Toro doing a Star Wars film or series were true, we have an update today from the director himself. Though fans want him to touch every property, Del Toro is best known for his own style; even his Hellboy movies are arguably closer to his sensibility than Mike Mignola's. Star Wars , generally, is a pretty specific franchise in terms of style and not very much like Del Toro's films. He was at one point interested in developing a Jabba the Hutt movie , which would suit his tastes for monsters and drippy, rusty production design.

As for del Toro, he wants to clear the air about any rumors involving him and franchises. In a recent post on X, he declared, "Just some facts (some will take this denial as confirmation, I know) I am not in talks with any Star Wars, Marvel properties in any capacity." He clarified he's working on a script of his own, prepping a new stop-motion movie, and producing some things for others. That said, he did offer a tease about that Jabba the Hutt film that fell through.

Just some facts (some will take this denial as confirmation, I know) I am not in talks with any Star Wars, Marvel properties in any capacity. At all. I am involved in writing a screenplay, prepping my stop motion movie at Shadwomachine, producing a few things for others and…

Del Toro went on to confirm he co-wrote a script with David Goyer for a film called The Rise and Fall of Jabba the Hutt , and develop some art and sculptures, but that was as far as it went. While it sounds intriguing on the surface, Jabba is not necessarily the best protagonist around whom to base a movie — he speaks a fictional language most of the time, and he's basically a jerk. Maybe we could have seen a nicer side in interactions with son Rotta, but Rotta, even in his limited screen time, was a more compelling character.

It would be cool to see some of that artwork surface one day. The underworld corners of the Star Wars universe tend to be the most creative, unbound by the primal good versus evil Jedi/Sith dynamic. Given the degree to which Dave Filoni tends to repurpose every unused idea, however, the concepts could show up elsewhere without our even knowing it. Guillermo del Toro, meanwhile, is looking to segue into animation full-time .

Goyer and I did write the script and I even developed some art and sculptures… The Rise and Fall of Jabba the Hutt, it was called… https://t.co/jQ4K8GanID

Honestly, the best Star Wars movies aren't made by distinctive genre auteurs. Irvin Kershner directed The Empire Strikes Back , which is generally the favorite, and he was mostly channeling what George Lucas wanted. Rian Johnson tried to break the mold a bit with The Last Jedi , and made a film so divisive people are probably gearing up to argue about it in the comments below already. Del Toro's original sci-fi concept, Pacific Rim , spawned a sequel and a ton of merchandise; it didn't need to be part of any other pre-existing world. He was attached to the video game Silent Hills at one point , but that never ended up getting made, and he more recently declared himself done with video games and video game-based movies.

Are you sorry to hear that GDT won't be franchising any time soon? Or did you want that Jabba movie to happen? Slither down to comments and let us know.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google While fans are awaiting Witch Hat Atelier Season 2, the anime drops a gorgeous new visual of Qifrey. Witch Hat Atelier is easily one of the biggest anime of the year, and fans will see the return of their beloved characters next year. Produced by studio BUG FILMS, this breathtaking anime is based on the manga written and illustrated by Kamone Shirahama , which has been serialized in Kodansha’s seinen magazine Morning Two since 2016. The first season has only introduced the premise of this whimsical fantasy, but things will get more intense in the sequel season.

One of the characters at the center of attention will be Qifrey, who became a fan-favorite after the anime debut. Whether it's his moral ambiguity, his skills, or his goal that he is desperate to accomplish, everything about him easily makes him the most captivating character in the story. November 19th is his birthday, and to commemorate the special day, Kairi Unabara drew a gorgeous visual of Qifrey holding a bouquet of flowers. Unabara serves as the Chief Animation Director and the character designer of the anime. The birthday visual was shared by the official X handle of the anime , which immediately went viral as fans can't help but adore Unabara's stunning art style.

So far, the anime has only confirmed a 2027 release window, but it has yet to lock down an exact release date. Fans don't even know which season's lineup will include the anime, but we can expect an update when next year begins. Additionally, the second season will be streaming on Crunchyroll, where you can also catch up with the first season to jog your memory. Before each anime season, Crunchyroll reveals a lineup that includes the release dates, the English dub confirmation, and the streaming timing. We can expect all streaming information related to Witch Hat Atelier Season 2 to be added on the website a few weeks ahead of the premiere.

The anime ended its first season on a major cliffhanger in the middle of an attack in the Serpentback Cave. The story takes a turn for the worse in the finale since it's evident Qifrey needs to fight his hardest to keep his apprentices safe. A teaser was also revealed along with the second season announcement in June this year, which shared a glimpse at a dark appearance of Coco.

This clearly means she will be tapping into a new kind of power that she might not have enough control over. The story finally took shape in the first season, but it keeps gradually building up the fact that the world of magic has something much darker and dangerous lurking around. Coco and her fellow apprentices will definitely break more norms and tap into more secrets of the world.

articles.title: Robert Pattinson’s Bond Ascent: How Pricey Screen Tests and Amazon Execs Landed a Starry 007
articles.summary: What does an actor do in the quiet moments before the announcement that will change his life? For Robert Pattinson, there were about 12 hours between the Sunday phone call confirming he’d landed the role of James Bond and Amazon MGM’s Monday-morning release of the first image of the actor rocking a tuxedo and pistol. […]
articles.content:
What does an actor do in the quiet moments before the announcement that will change his life?

For Robert Pattinson , there were about 12 hours between the Sunday phone call confirming he’d landed the role of James Bond and Amazon MGM’s Monday-morning release of the first image of the actor rocking a tuxedo and pistol. He spent it, rather predictably, watching an arthouse horror film. Related Stories 'Cher Adores Michael Douglas,' Icon's Rep Says After Douglas Disses Her Oscar Win for 'Moonstruck' Harry Styles, Billie Eilish, Sam Fender and Cher to Headline Glastonbury Festival

His longtime friend and collaborator Robert Eggers told Variety this week that Pattinson was screening the director’s forthcoming genre drama “Werwulf” when the Bond news broke. Nothing like a stark naked Aaron Taylor-Johnson terrorizing a quaint village to pass the time. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

But after months (years, really) of toiling and speculation over who would replace Daniel Craig in the film adaptations of Ian Fleming’s spy novels, Pattinson took the crown. It buttons up a delicious, messy and very public guessing game over which lucky man would land the iconic role. When Amazon MGM bought out rights to James Bond from longtime custodians the Broccoli family in 2025, intentions were set for a young star who could shoulder the franchise for a decade or two. An A-list team of producers (Amy Pascal of “Spider-Man” and David Heyman of the “Harry Potter” movies) recruited Denis Villeneuve to direct. Together, with significant influence from Amazon execs Courtenay Valenti and Mike Hopkins (and yes, Jeff Bezos), they screen-tested a laundry list of virile performers — including Callum Turner, Tom Francis, Jack Lowden and Josh O’Connor — earlier this year.

For the curious, the batch of screen tests cost Amazon MGM between $300,000 and $500,000 to pull off, ostensibly in secret (everyone found out), sources familiar with the process say. But two wildcard actors who tested at the last minute — “Superman” star Nicholas Hoult and the DCU’s reining Batman, Pattinson — tipped the scales. Villeneuve’s voice became the most trusted in the room on the matter of Bond’s casting, two insiders tell Variety . blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

His shorthand with Pattinson from working on “Dune: Part Three” made the choice inevitable, according to industry insiders — especially after Turner, the early favorite, came under scrutiny against more established names like Hoult and Pattinson. Lowden, the heat-seeking star of “Slow Horses,” was even the subject of a suspected sabotage campaign when paparazzi footage circulated showed the actor bungling an on-set motorcycle stunt just two weeks before the Bond casting was confirmed.

A sect of the internet lost its mind when Variety reported earlier this month that Harry Styles and Theo James were both in talks for the role. It’s rare, even by tentpole movie standards, that such a long list of candidates would flow so freely through public channels. The studios hate it because it makes them seem indecisive, one exec says. Talent absolutely hates it because the also-rans will have to answer for almost being James Bond on talk show couches and podcasts for the next 10 years.

“Whatever, it’s really fun,” one top talent rep tells Variety of the audition merry-go-round.

While there will be detractors, it’s inarguable that the Bond gig now enshrines Pattinson in the upper echelons of movie stardom. He was already well on his way, with even civilian social media pundits having commented on the “generational run” Pattinson has been living out onscreen in films like “Primetime,” “The Odyssey,” “The Drama,” “Die My Love” and, obviously, “The Batman.” That’s to say nothing of the deeply indie era (“Good Time,” “The Lighthouse”) that followed major franchise moments like his star-making turn in the “Twilight Saga” movies and a prominent role in “Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire.” The new job also represents a major win for Pattinson’s agent of more than 20 years, Stephanie Ritz of WME. Ritz and team have managed to populate massive IP with Pattinson’s face while still allowing the actor to take risks and brand himself a maverick for the cross-generational devotees of studios like A24.

Given the shocking November news that DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran had been jettisoned by the David Ellison regime, it’s doubtful Pattinson would linger long as Matt Reeves’ caped crusader — freeing him up to embody the sultry British charm and execute the bare-knuckle action audiences have come to expect from 007. Art-house horror movies may have to take a back seat.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Cartoon Network has been an icon of animation history since its launch in 1992, with it releasing popular shows throughout the decades like Dexter's Laboratory , Samurai Jack , Ben 10 , Adventure Time , and more. One of the company's most beloved shows just celebrated its anniversary, reminding viewers of one of Cartoon Network's earliest and best original series.

Superheroes have been a staple of Cartoon Network since the beginning , from acquired programming like Super Friends to original shows like Teen Titans Go! . However, it is impossible to deny that their most famous superhero series is Craig McCracken's 1998 masterpiece, The Powerpuff Girls .

While a student at the California Institute of the Arts, Craig McCracken developed a series titled Whoopass Stew! , a parody of the superhero shows of the 1960s that followed three little girls who are granted extraordinary powers when the professor accidentally adds a can of whoopass to his experiment. The short, titled "A Sticky Situation," was well-received enough to land McCracken a pitch meeting at Hanna-Barbera. After the project was reworked as The Powerpuff Girls , two shorts were produced for Cartoon Network's World Premiere Toons block. The first of these, "Meat Fuzzy Lumpkins," aired on February 20, 1995, while the second, "Crime 101," aired on January 28, 1996. Unfortunately, the shorts didn't get picked up for a series, and McCracken went on to work for Genndy Tartakovsky on Dexter's Laboratory . While there, McCracken was then allowed to pitch The Powerpuff Girls again, and in 1997, the series was greenlit.

On November 18, 1998, The Powerpuff Girls premiered on Cartoon Network, with the premiere consisting of the segments "Monkey See, Doggie Do" and "Mommy Fearest." The show was a hit, with it being the highest-rated premiere of a Cartoon Network series at the time of its airing. The show received incredible viewership numbers across children and adult audiences, something that surprised the network due to the show being designed to appeal to young viewers. However, the series' critical and commercial success allowed it to run for six seasons, and the series ended on March 25, 2005, with the release of its 78th episode.

The Powerpuff Girls has become an icon of animation, allowing its influence to far outlast the show's original run. The franchise has come back for several other projects, including the 2002 The Powerpuff Girls Movie and the 2006 anime Powerpuff Girls Z . Two specials have been produced since the show's cancellation, such as the half-hour 2009 episode "The Powerpuff Girls Rule!!!" and the 2014 CGI special Powerpuff Girls: Dance Pantsed . Most interestingly, a live-action sequel series was in development at The CW, starring Chloe Bennet, Dove Cameron, and Yana Perrault as Blossom, Bubbles, and Buttercup, respectively. However, the series was cancelled before release due to negative reviews.

The Powerpuff Girls has maintained its popularity more than two decades after the show's cancellation, with merchandise and memes spawned from the franchise still being all over the place. It could be argued that The Powerpuff Girls is Cartoon Network's most iconic show of all time, with it helping to define the channel's original programming in its early days and influencing the entire field of animation.

The Powerpuff Girls is a historic show for many reasons, but one of the show's most notable facts is rarely discussed. Hanna-Barbera Productions, named for founders William Hanna and Joseph Barbera, helped create the field of television animation in the early 1950s and 60s. Shows like The Huckleberry Hound Show , The Flintstones , Scooby-Doo, Where Are You? , and more are still well-known today , having become some of the company's most popular programs. However, The Powerpuff Girls often isn't lumped in with these Hanna-Barbera programs, despite the fact that it was a Hanna-Barbera Show.

The Powerpuff Girls was the final Hanna-Barbera series to premiere, with its first four seasons being produced by the company. Seasons 5 and 6 were produced by Cartoon Network Studios after Hanna-Barbera was absorbed into Warner Bros. Animation in 2001. This makes The Powerpuff Girls a milestone in the history of animation, with it marking the end of the Hanna-Barbera era and the beginning of Cartoon Network. It is hard to deny the impact that the show has had since its premiere, and it is still beloved by many 28 years after its started.

The host has long been known for his sportscasting and "The Rich Eisen Show" has long been featured as part of sports programming, but that doesn't mean the host and the program can't take a detour once in a while.

"This is what our show is about. It's a pop culture show," Eisen says during a recent interview. "Sports is just one spoke on the pop culture wheel." U2 holds forth with Eisen on Friday's program.

Eisen has over the years talked with Jon Bon Jovi, Jodie Foster, James Taylor, Will Ferrell, Kenny Chesney and Snoop Dogg, and there are reasons for him to do so. How did Eisen's team land U2? The band, which just released its first full album, Carnaval de Luz, in nine years, is scheduled to play the halftime show of Netflix's stream of a Thanksgiving Eve game taking place between the Green Day Packers and the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium. That's not too far from the studio that houses Eisen's show. A producer called. The band's publicist seemed willing.

Eisen says he didn't spend hours trying to come up with questions that would ferret out some small detail that fans don't already know. Instead, his focus is on trying to create "a good hang."

Giant K-pop show the MAMA Awards 2026 is taking place in Osaka, Japan, this weekend,a and the first winners have been crowed.

BTS won the coveted Artist of the Year category for the eighth time, and Enhypen won three: Fans' Choice of the Year, Favorite M-Countdown Stage and Fan's Choice Top 10 - Male. Ive won Best Female Group.

The music event, which broadcasts in Korea on Mnet , brings together Korean music performers from across generations over two nights.

"MAMA Awards has grown alongside K-POP’s global growth, we believe these efforts have created more ways for artists and fans around the world to connect," said Yoon Shin Hye, who is head of CJ ENM -owned Mnet.

“Over the past 27 years, MAMA Awards has expanded its stages to places it had never been, connected artists and fans in ways never seen before, and been the first to show K-pop’s new possibilities," added Harry H.K. Shin, Head of Music Entertainment at CJ ENM in a statement. "All of that was possible with our one firm belief: 'Music Makes One.'
